reviewer: Codex (AI editorial review; not human approval)
interpretation: These nine explicit decisions supersede the pending withdrawals preserved below. The earlier fifteen-entry correction history remains unchanged. Eight inherited families are authored; explore is retained as whole-stem exposure after an individual review of competing historical accounts.

etym-compare-hold9.title: Online Etymology Dictionary: compare
etym-compare-hold9.author: Douglas Harper
etym-compare-hold9.sections: Entry history and linked family evidence
etym-compare-hold9.evidence: The entry identifies com- with par equal through Latin comparare and French comparer. It dates the comparison of similarities and differences as a conventional extension of the earlier equality relation; current comparison does not assert that the compared objects are equal.

etym-investigate-hold9.title: Online Etymology Dictionary: investigate
etym-investigate-hold9.author: Douglas Harper
etym-investigate-hold9.sections: Entry history and linked family evidence
etym-investigate-hold9.evidence: Two routes into English are offered: back-formation from investigation or borrowing of the Latin participial form. Both retain the in- and vestigium track family. The entry distinguishes vestigium from the unrelated clothing root vestis.

etym-suggest-hold9.title: Online Etymology Dictionary: suggest
etym-suggest-hold9.author: Douglas Harper
etym-suggest-hold9.sections: Entry history and linked family evidence
etym-suggest-hold9.evidence: The history and linked suggestion discussion give sub- with gerere through suggestus. They trace the transition from supplying or bringing forward to proposing an idea; the modern proposal sense is not a literal carrying task.

etym-explore-hold9.title: Online Etymology Dictionary: explore
etym-explore-hold9.author: Douglas Harper
etym-explore-hold9.sections: Entry history and linked family evidence
etym-explore-hold9.evidence: The entry offers back-formation from exploration or borrowing via French. It discusses the historical plorare cry-out account but also a competing pluere flow account. That uncertainty and the established explore/exploration base argue against presenting one deep historical split as the uniquely settled learner graph.

etym-separate-hold9.title: Online Etymology Dictionary: separate
etym-separate-hold9.author: Douglas Harper
etym-separate-hold9.sections: Entry history and linked family evidence
etym-separate-hold9.evidence: The verb derives from the Latin participial form separatus, with se- apart and parare prepare/procure. The adjective has related borrowing/conversion history. This evidence supports the selected verb graph while keeping par.prepare distinct from compare par.equal.

etym-multiply-hold9.title: Online Etymology Dictionary: multiply
etym-multiply-hold9.author: Douglas Harper
etym-multiply-hold9.sections: Entry history and linked family evidence
etym-multiply-hold9.evidence: The entry traces the verb through French multiplier to Latin multiplicare and multiplex, linking the many element and fold family. The arithmetic sense is explicitly historical; no adverbial -ly analysis is licensed.

etym-divide-hold9.title: Online Etymology Dictionary: divide
etym-divide-hold9.author: Douglas Harper
etym-divide-hold9.sections: Entry history and linked family evidence
etym-divide-hold9.evidence: The entry identifies the assimilated dis- prefix plus a separate-root -videre, with an arithmetic extension. The separate root is not the Latin sight root used in video and vision.

etym-estimate-hold9.title: Online Etymology Dictionary: estimate
etym-estimate-hold9.author: Douglas Harper
etym-estimate-hold9.sections: Entry history and linked family evidence
etym-estimate-hold9.evidence: The verb is traced to Latin aestimatus/aestimare, valuing or appraising. Its current approximate-judgment meaning developed later. The esteem relation is historical; the target remains approximation rather than respectful admiration.

etym-retire-hold9.title: Online Etymology Dictionary: retire
etym-retire-hold9.author: Douglas Harper
etym-retire-hold9.sections: Entry history and linked family evidence
etym-retire-hold9.evidence: The entry gives French re- back plus tirer draw and explicitly traces withdrawal from employment as an extension of drawing back. It supports the career sense without substituting English tire weary.

etym-ate-hold9.title: Online Etymology Dictionary: -ate
etym-ate-hold9.author: Douglas Harper
etym-ate-hold9.sections: Entry history and linked family evidence
etym-ate-hold9.evidence: The entry distinguishes the inherited noun/adjective ending from the English verbal -ate formation based on Latin participial stems. Separate is a named related form. This licenses an inherited verbal ending, not automatic stripping of every final ate string.

etym-sub-hold9.title: Online Etymology Dictionary: sub-
etym-sub-hold9.author: Douglas Harper
etym-sub-hold9.sections: Entry history and linked family evidence
etym-sub-hold9.evidence: Latin sub- assimilates to following g and other consonants. The entry explicitly includes suggest among borrowed words whose historical prefix contribution is no longer transparent.

etym-se-hold9.title: Online Etymology Dictionary: se-
etym-se-hold9.author: Douglas Harper
etym-se-hold9.sections: Entry history and linked family evidence
etym-se-hold9.evidence: The entry records the apart/away prefix in Latin-derived English words. This is the specific se- identity selected for separate, not an arbitrary opening syllable.

etym-tire-hold9.title: Online Etymology Dictionary: tire
etym-tire-hold9.author: Douglas Harper
etym-tire-hold9.sections: Entry history and linked family evidence
etym-tire-hold9.evidence: The fatigue verb comes from Old English teorian, a different history from the French drawing element in retire. The wheel noun has a separate equipment/attire history and is also excluded.

mw-par-hold9.title: Merriam-Webster: par
mw-par-hold9.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-par-hold9.evidence: The equality noun is traced to Latin par equal and the child-oriented history explicitly connects it to compare. This supports par.equal, not pare trimming or parare preparation.

mw-prepare-hold9.title: Merriam-Webster: prepare
mw-prepare-hold9.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-prepare-hold9.evidence: The history identifies prae- plus parare supply/provide/make ready, providing a companion family for the prepare/procure element of separate. It is unrelated to compare par equal.

mw-ingest-hold9.title: Merriam-Webster: ingest
mw-ingest-hold9.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-ingest-hold9.evidence: The history gives ingestus from in- plus gerere bear/carry, corroborating the recurring gest realization independently of the unrelated modern noun gest.

mw-dis-hold9.title: Merriam-Webster: dis-
mw-dis-hold9.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-dis-hold9.evidence: The prefix history explicitly gives Latin di- before v among the variants of dis- apart/asunder. This supports the exact di surface in divide and distinguishes it from the numeral di- two.

mw-multi-hold9.title: Merriam-Webster: multi-
mw-multi-hold9.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-multi-hold9.evidence: The combining form supplies the many/multiple contribution and is traced to Latin multus. This is the numeric element in multiply rather than an arbitrary multi syllable sequence.

collins-sug-hold9.title: Collins: sug-
collins-sug-hold9.author: Webster's New World College Dictionary editors; HarperCollins
collins-sug-hold9.evidence: The entry explicitly identifies sug- as the before-g form of sub- and uses suggest as its example. The unrelated sales acronym is not selected.

pearson-ply-hold9.title: Vocabulary Their Way, chapter 6: Teaching Content-Specific Academic Vocabulary
pearson-ply-hold9.author: Shane Templeton, Donald R. Bear, Francine Johnston, and Marcia Invernizzi
pearson-ply-hold9.sections: Printed pages 110 and 130; mathematics root table and Origin of Multiply
pearson-ply-hold9.evidence: The publisher-hosted chapter explicitly associates plic/ply with the fold family in multiply/multiplication and discusses this family as vocabulary instruction. The game retains the actual mathematical definition rather than teaching that every multiplication makes a number larger or requires physical folding.

michigan-ate-hold9.title: ELI 538: Rules and Practices, Rule 6-3
michigan-ate-hold9.author: University of Michigan English Language Institute; page cites Linda Grant, Well Said, 2nd edition
michigan-ate-hold9.evidence: This teaching resource explicitly treats estimate as a verb with -ate and contrasts its noun/verb pronunciations. Its exercise also places separate in the -ate family. This is term-level evidence for an English suffix boundary, not just a Latin derivation.

thoughtful-vestig-hold9.title: Prefixes, Roots, and Suffixes
thoughtful-vestig-hold9.author: Thoughtful Learning editorial team
thoughtful-vestig-hold9.evidence: The educational root list explicitly identifies vestig trace in investigate, vestige, and vestigial. This supports the retained vestig teaching unit while the dictionary establishes the in- and verbal formation.

mw-compare-new.title: Merriam-Webster: compare
mw-compare-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-compare-new.sections: Word History and relevant current sense
mw-compare-new.evidence: The current comparison sense matches the target. The history identifies com- plus par equal through comparare; this is distinct from English pare trim and the prepare root in separate.

mw-com-prefix-new.title: Merriam-Webster: com-
mw-com-prefix-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-com-prefix-new.evidence: The prefix expresses with/together and explicitly lists con- as a variant. This supports com-/con in connect.

anderson-2e-roots-new.title: Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd edition, section 5.2: Roots, bases, and affixes
anderson-2e-roots-new.author: Catherine Anderson, Bronwyn Bjorkman, Derek Denis, Julianne Doner, Margaret Grant, Nathan Sanders, and Ai Taniguchi
anderson-2e-roots-new.sections: Affixes vs roots; Free and bound morphemes
anderson-2e-roots-new.evidence: The author text distinguishes roots from bases and affixes and recognizes bound roots. It also separates historical source-language complexity from a contemporary speaker's analysis, using library and nation as examples. Neither free-base absence nor historical complexity alone decides a teaching graph.

mw-investigate-new.title: Merriam-Webster: investigate
mw-investigate-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-investigate-new.sections: Word History and relevant current sense
mw-investigate-new.evidence: The history derives the word through investigatus/investigare from in- and vestigium, footprint or track. It establishes a real historical family but does not by itself settle the intended English three-part graph.

mw-vestige-new.title: Merriam-Webster: vestige
mw-vestige-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-vestige-new.sections: Word History and relevant current sense
mw-vestige-new.evidence: The history independently traces vestige to Latin vestigium, footprint or trace. The relation is real; the precise vestig/vestige realization and English investigate suffix analysis still require a decision.

mw-ate-suffix-new.title: Merriam-Webster: -ate
mw-ate-suffix-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-ate-suffix-new.evidence: The dictionary distinguishes a verb-forming suffix and traces it to Latin participial morphology. This is background evidence for investigate, separate, and estimate research, not term-level authorization for automatic splitting.

mw-suggest-new.title: Merriam-Webster: suggest
mw-suggest-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-suggest-new.sections: Word History and relevant current sense
mw-suggest-new.evidence: The proposing sense is explicit. The history identifies sub- plus gerere carry via the participial form suggestus. The sug-/gest realization is a valid research lead, not evidence for unrelated modern sug or gest words.

mw-explore-new.title: Merriam-Webster: explore
mw-explore-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-explore-new.sections: Word History and relevant current sense
mw-explore-new.evidence: The history identifies ex- plus plorare cry out. The selected examining/learning sense is semantically distant; historical segmentation alone does not settle an appropriate modern teaching graph.

mw-separate-new.title: Merriam-Webster: separate
mw-separate-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-separate-new.sections: Word History and relevant current sense
mw-separate-new.evidence: The history identifies se- apart plus parare prepare/procure. That prepare root differs from the equal par root in compare; a spelling-only shared canonical identity would be wrong.

mw-multiply-new.title: Merriam-Webster: multiply
mw-multiply-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-multiply-new.sections: Word History and relevant current sense
mw-multiply-new.evidence: The arithmetic verb is traced through French multiplier and Latin multiplicare to multiplex. This establishes the multiple family but not a direct English multi plus the layer verb ply exercise.

mw-multiple-new.title: Merriam-Webster: multiple
mw-multiple-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-multiple-new.sections: Word History and relevant current sense
mw-multiple-new.evidence: The history identifies Latin multi- plus -plex meaning fold. The relationship to multiply is documented, while the exact English plex/plic/ply realization remains to be authored.

mw-divide-new.title: Merriam-Webster: divide
mw-divide-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-divide-new.sections: Word History and relevant current sense
mw-divide-new.evidence: The arithmetic sense is explicit. The history identifies dis- plus a Latin -videre separate root, distinct from Latin videre see. No free English vide is needed for a possible bound-root analysis.

mw-estimate-new.title: Merriam-Webster: estimate
mw-estimate-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-estimate-new.sections: Word History and relevant current sense
mw-estimate-new.evidence: The history gives Latin aestimatus/aestimare value or estimate. It confirms a historical verbal formation but does not settle whether the intended English lesson should expose estim plus -ate.

mw-retire-new.title: Merriam-Webster: retire
mw-retire-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-retire-new.sections: Word History and relevant current sense
mw-retire-new.evidence: The history identifies French re- plus tirer draw. The career-ending sense must not be analyzed using modern tire fatigue; a draw-root proposal needs explicit treatment of the historical tire/tir realization.

mw-re-prefix-new.title: Merriam-Webster: re-
mw-re-prefix-new.author: Merriam-Webster editors
mw-re-prefix-new.evidence: The prefix distinguishes again from back/backward. The revised receive and reflect candidates select the historical back identity, not a productive repetition claim.

changes.boundary_note: Canonical par, surface pare; the explicit whole output is compare.

review.reason: Reopened after new term-specific evidence: The com- plus par equal family is documented, so the prior no-modern-com/pare argument is insufficient. Hold until the exact English par/pare realization and learner-level comparison meaning are authored and independently checked. Do not confuse equal par with pare trim or prepare par in separate.

review.reviewer: Codex (AI editorial review; not human approval)
review.method: Individual contemporary-sense analysis with named framework and lexical evidence; no suffix inference or generated review.
review.rationale: The selected comparison action uses the inherited com- and par equal family. Its exact English root surface is pare; final e belongs to this authored realization and is not a third morpheme. The par.equal identity is corroborated by par and kept distinct from pare trim and separate par.prepare. Comparing can establish differences as well as similarities; it does not assert equality. The completed current meaning is preserved, and this graph does not claim a productive English com- plus free pare construction.

review.reason: Reopened after new term-specific evidence: The in- and vestigium track family is documented. Hold the prior whole-form proposal and do not yet serialize in + vestig + -ate: the exact English stem realization, prefix contribution, and inherited verbal ending require a term-specific graph decision.

proposed_entry.meaning: Examine something to find out more

review.reviewer: Codex (AI editorial review; not human approval)
review.method: Individual contemporary-sense analysis with named framework and lexical evidence; no suffix inference or generated review.
review.rationale: The individually attested family combines in- into with vestig track/trace and inherited verbal -ate. The teaching source explicitly lists vestig in investigate and vestige. The graph first builds the bound stem investig, then the complete verb; investig is not presented as an independent English word. Both proposed routes into English, borrowing and back-formation from investigation, share this family, so the graph does not assert a unique chronology. The selected careful inquiry sense remains authoritative; there is no clothing vest root or invented free vestigate requirement.

changes.boundary_note: Canonical sub-, surface sug; gest retains the carry family.

before_entry.meaning: Put forward an idea to consider

review.reason: Reopened after new term-specific evidence: The sub-/gerere family and suggestus are documented. Hold while the sug-/gest allomorphs and the furnish/propose semantic development are checked as teaching units; the old whole-form justification cannot be based on missing free sug or gest words.

proposed_entry.meaning: Put forward an idea to consider

review.reviewer: Codex (AI editorial review; not human approval)
review.method: Individual contemporary-sense analysis with named framework and lexical evidence; no suffix inference or generated review.
review.rationale: Collins explicitly records sug- as the before-g allomorph of sub- in suggest. The suggest/ingest histories corroborate gest as the participial realization of the carry/bear family. Sub.under is a historical identity here, not a claim that proposing an idea literally means carrying something underneath. The dictionary traces the furnishing/bringing-forward development into the selected proposal sense. The graph neither selects the modern sales acronym sug nor treats the unrelated noun gest as its base.

changes.boundary_note: One complete current stem; no composition mastery. Historical alternatives remain in the review record.

before_entry.meaning: Look around to learn about something

review.reason: Reopened after new term-specific evidence: The ex-/plorare cry-out history is documented but distant from the target examining/learning sense. Hold both a reflexive whole-form declaration and a literal out-plus-cry exercise. A reviewer must decide contemporary learner depth with the explore/exploration family and historical opacity made explicit.

proposed_entry.meaning: Look around to learn about something

review.reviewer: Codex (AI editorial review; not human approval)
review.method: Individual contemporary-sense analysis with named framework and lexical evidence; no suffix inference or generated review.
review.rationale: Keep the current explore stem whole at this teaching depth after examining, rather than denying, its historical complexity. The new history offers back-formation from exploration or borrowing and records competing cry-out and flow explanations of the deeper element. The stable contemporary family is explore/explorer/exploration; neither disputed historical account supplies a uniquely settled ex-plus-root lesson for the selected examining/discovery sense. This deliberate whole-stem exposure does not claim that bound roots must be free words or that explore has no etymological structure. A future explicit historical-family lesson may revisit it with the competing account retained.

changes.boundary_note: se + par -> separ (bound intermediate); separ + ate -> separate.

before_entry.meaning: Move things apart from each other

review.reason: Reopened after new term-specific evidence: The se- apart plus parare prepare family is documented. Hold until the English se/par/ate realization and nonliteral prepare element are resolved. A future par.prepare identity must stay separate from par.equal in compare.

proposed_entry.meaning: Move things apart from each other

review.reviewer: Codex (AI editorial review; not human approval)
review.method: Individual contemporary-sense analysis with named framework and lexical evidence; no suffix inference or generated review.
review.rationale: The selected verb has the inherited se- apart, par prepare/procure, and verbal -ate structure. Prepare supplies the companion parare family, and the University of Michigan teaching exercise independently includes separate in the -ate family. The exact first join is the bound stem separ, not an invented standalone verb; the second yields separate. Par.prepare is kept distinct from compare par.equal. The whole separating action remains the definition; the historical preparation gloss is not a claim that separation means preparation or equalization. This review concerns the verb rather than automatically reusing its analysis for a noun or adjective sense.

changes.boundary_note: multi + ply -> multiply; preserve ply as one root realization, with no separate y ending.

before_entry.meaning: Add equal groups to find a total

review.reason: Reopened after new term-specific evidence: The multi-/plex fold family is documented through multiple and multiplicare. Hold while plex/plic/ply and the verb ending are resolved. Neither a missing free arithmetic ply nor the existence of the modern layer verb settles the graph.

proposed_entry.meaning: Add equal groups to find a total

review.reviewer: Codex (AI editorial review; not human approval)
review.method: Individual contemporary-sense analysis with named framework and lexical evidence; no suffix inference or generated review.
review.rationale: The publisher-hosted Vocabulary Their Way chapter explicitly teaches the plic/ply fold family in multiply and multiplication. Together with the word history and multi- entry this supports the exact multi plus ply graph. Ply is the inherited fold-family root, not a substituted modern layer noun or a verb about plying a trade. The full ply surface includes the inherited English realization; no detachable y or adverbial -ly is invented. Multiplication retains its arithmetic definition, including cases that do not increase a number, and the historical folding analogy does not replace that definition.

changes.boundary_note: Canonical dis-, surface di; bound vide.separate is distinct from sight and numeral identities.

before_entry.meaning: Split a number into equal groups

review.reason: Reopened after new term-specific evidence: The dictionary identifies dis- plus a separate-root -videre. Hold until di/dis and vid/vide are authored and independently checked; do not confuse this root with Latin videre see. Lack of a free English vide cannot justify atomic status.

proposed_entry.meaning: Split a number into equal groups

review.reviewer: Codex (AI editorial review; not human approval)
review.method: Individual contemporary-sense analysis with named framework and lexical evidence; no suffix inference or generated review.
review.rationale: The word history identifies dis- apart and the separate-root -videre. The prefix history explicitly records the di- realization before v, supporting di plus vide with the final e retained in the authored English root surface. The vide.separate identity is distinct from the vid/vis sight family and di is not the numeral combining form meaning two. The arithmetic sense is a conventional application of division into parts; the graph preserves its current definition without requiring a free English vide word.

changes.boundary_note: estim + ate -> estimate; the selected target is the verb, with its existing audio unchanged.

review.reason: Reopened after new term-specific evidence: The Latin aestimare/aestimatus family is established. Hold the old whole-form rationale while a reviewer determines whether estim and -ate are appropriate English teaching units; not having a free estim word is not decisive.

review.reviewer: Codex (AI editorial review; not human approval)
review.method: Individual contemporary-sense analysis with named framework and lexical evidence; no suffix inference or generated review.
review.rationale: The history gives the aestimare/aestimatus valuing and appraising family, realized as estim in this inherited English form. The University of Michigan resource specifically identifies estimate as a verbal -ate example and contrasts it with the noun pronunciation. This term-level evidence supports estim plus -ate rather than a spelling-only suffix guess. Estim is bound, and no independent estim word is required. The selected informed approximation sense remains the whole meaning; the graph does not substitute the respectful-admiration sense of esteem or invent an es- prefix.

changes.boundary_note: Canonical tir, surface tire; re.back + tir.draw -> retire, with no fatigue or repetition identity.

Hold the prior whole-form proposal until historical tir/tire draw and career withdrawal are explicitly assessed. The unrelated English fatigue verb cannot serve as the component, but that does not make the word morphologically indivisible.

proposed_entry.meaning: Stop working after a long career

review.reviewer: Codex (AI editorial review; not human approval)
review.method: Individual contemporary-sense analysis with named framework and lexical evidence; no suffix inference or generated review.
review.rationale: The dictionary history explicitly traces retire through French re- back and tirer draw into withdrawal from employment. The graph uses canonical tir.draw with the inherited English tire surface; final e belongs to that realization. This is not the Old English fatigue verb tire, the wheel noun, or a productive instruction to become tired again. The selected retirement sense remains the complete definition. Bound historical tir is legitimate even without a current free drawing verb of that spelling, and its canonical identity remains separate from all fatigue and equipment senses.
